coverage.note: Four items named no San Francisco building: two AI-funding stories, an Atherton house sale on the Peninsula that is also a private individual's home, and an eviction story that names neither an address nor a building and whose subject is a person.

findings.description: A one-alarm fire broke out in a fourth-floor apartment somewhere on this block early on 30 August 2026; the fire department declared a mass-casualty incident and five people were taken to hospital. The article states that the building involved has not been identified publicly. Nobody involved is recorded here.

citation.label: Hoodline, “Mission Street Fire Sends 4 to Hospital as Crews Assess Other Residents,” 30 August 2026

raw.text: The cause of the fire and the exact building involved have not been detailed publicly.

resolution.method: The story gives a block, not an address, and says so itself. Every numbered address in it belongs to a different building: 1800 Mission Street is the National Guard Armory, named as the landmark the block sits near; 2300 Folsom Street is Fire Station 7, named as the firehouse that would answer the call; 2001 Potrero Avenue is the hospital such patients are usually taken to. None of the three is the building that burned.
resolution.note: A fire is exactly the kind of event this module exists for, and this one still cannot be placed. If a later story names the building, it will be publishable then.

publish.note: No building to put it on. Recorded rather than dropped so the next reader knows that 1800 Mission Street — which the site has a page for — is the Armory next door and not the building that burned; that is the mistake this finding exists to prevent.
